verdict.rationale: Google's docs say signing in to a Google Account in Authenticator syncs verification codes across all your devices, and codes sync automatically when you sign in on a new device. This covers phone and tablet sync. The only platform evidence describes mobile implementations, so there is no evidence of a computer or desktop client. The community complaints about missing backups predate or concern other features and do not contradict cloud sync. Missing for 10: evidence of a computer/desktop client receiving synced codes, detail on real-time simultaneous sync behavior, independent hands-on corroboration of multi-device sync.

support.subject: As an everyday user, my tokens are available on my phone, tablet, and computer at the same time, kept in sync automatically

citations.quote: With Google Authenticator, you can synchronize your verification codes across all your devices, simply by signing in to your Google Account.
When you sign in to your Google Account within Google Authenticator on a new device, your codes are automatically synced to this device.
The Google Authenticator project includes implementations of one-time passcode generators for several mobile platforms.
